summary: Lists magic variables that users can't set, including ansible_check_mode, ansible_collection_name, ansible_config_file, ansible_dependent_role_names, ansible_diff_mode, ansible_forks, ansible_index_var, ansible_inventory_sources, ansible_limit, ansible_loop, ansible_loop_var, and ansible_parent_role_names.
questions: Which variable tells me if the playbook is in check mode?
How do I find out which ansible.cfg is being used from inside a playbook?
Is there a variable with the value of --limit?
How can a role know which role included it?
Can I set magic variables myself?
What variable holds the number of forks?

answer_card.title: Magic variables (part 1)
answer_card.answer_md:
Magic variables can't be set by users; Ansible always overrides them.
- `ansible_check_mode` / `ansible_diff_mode`: booleans for check/diff mode
- `ansible_collection_name`: collection of the running task (`namespace.collection`)
- `ansible_config_file`: full path of the config file in use
- `ansible_dependent_role_names`: roles imported as dependencies
- `ansible_forks`: max forks for this run
- `ansible_index_var` (2.9) / `ansible_loop_var` (2.8): names given to `loop_control.index_var` / `loop_var`
- `ansible_inventory_sources`: inventory sources used
- `ansible_limit`: contents of `--limit`
- `ansible_loop`: extended loop info when `loop_control.extended` is on
- `ansible_parent_role_names`: parent roles when run via `include_role`/`import_role`, most recent first
